newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes higher helped by banking issues.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes higher helped by banking issues.

text.p: The Czech PX50 stumbled its way to another small gain on Tuesday as a late rise in continuous trading by SPT Telecom complemented moderate gains for the index's two biggest banking issues.
The PX50 was up 0.4 percent at the close to 560.2.
Komercni Banka, with 11 percent of the PX50's capitalisation, rose five crowns to 2,368, while Ceska Sporitelna, with a 5.6 percent index capitalisation, rose two crowns to 326.
On Tuesday both banks recieved BBB- long term and A-3 short term counterparty ratings from Standard and Poors (S&P).
The ratings were the first of investment grade by S&P for Czech commercial banks.

S&P noted in its reports about Komercni and Sporitelna that the importance of the institutions to the Czech economy made it likely that government support for them would be forthcoming if the need ever arose.
"The implicit state interest in maintaining the health of its main banks is clear...and you can see that in what they did with Agrobanka," said Sandy Chen of CS First Boston.
Agrobanka, the largest fully private Czech bank, was aided by the central bank after running into liquidity problems last year.
Elswhere among the blue chips, SPT Telecom closed seven crowns higher at 3,397 while power utility CEZ dropped six crowns to 1,058.
